target_customer: Cardiologists and hospitals treating class III chronic heart failure patients (outpatient catheter procedure), paid by hospitals and ultimately payers
problem: Many chronic heart failure patients have limited options; the company argues that overactive sympathetic nerve signaling drives fluid buildup, and wants a safe, targeted ablation that confirms it worked.
business_model: Medical device sold to hospitals per procedure; pre-revenue and pre-clinical per sources found
product_category: Catheter-based nerve ablation medical device for heart failure

founders.name: Tyler Melton
prior_employers: Johnson & Johnson Center for Device Innovation
founders.background_notes: Source: healthcarediscovery.ai profile, which cites primary records. YC page lists him as the only founder.

founders.name: Ishan Kamat
education: MD and MBA; Baylor College of Medicine medical student at founding
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder-level leader on the company site (CMO) and the profile says he met Melton in the TMC Biodesign program. Not on the YC page.

investors: National Science Foundation SBIR Phase I

competitors.name: Axon Therapies
competitors.what: Catheter-based greater splanchnic nerve ablation for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (Satera system)
competitors.traction_then: Sham-controlled Rebalance-HF trial of 150 patients already enrolling

technical_complexity.rationale: A new catheter that ablates a specific nerve and verifies the result needs device engineering, animal studies, FDA pathway work and clinical data from a three person team.

defensibility.rationale: Regulatory clearance and clinical evidence are slow and costly to replicate, but a rival with a head start was already in human trials and the company's patents could not be confirmed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. A third party profile says that as of September 2026 no clinical trial was registered and the company has stayed small.

market_need_then: Heart failure is common and costly with limited device options; the neighbouring Rebalance-HF trial of splanchnic ablation was enrolling by December 2020, showing clinical and investor interest in the approach.

rebrands.why: Not stated; Caridian Medical, Inc. appears in the 2021 Form D and the 2023 NSF grant per the healthcarediscovery.ai profile

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand; search results mix it up with Corvia Medical, a different heart failure device company.

outcome_analysis: Corveus is a tiny Houston device startup that came out of the TMC Biodesign program, took YC in W22, and has funded itself through small private money, an NSF Phase I grant and prizes. A third party profile found no registered clinical trial or FDA authorization as of September 2026, and a competing splanchnic ablation trial reportedly showed no benefit over sham. The path to a venture sized round depends on first in human data that has not appeared.
notes: Melton said in a 2023 interview (search summary of a conference video) the first round was just under 900K to 1M USD; the Form D showed only 75K sold in October 2021, so the larger figure is unverified and not recorded as a round. Caplight lists 1.19M total and an accelerator round dated 2024-08, unverified. The 35K Texas A&M prize in 2023 and a 2024 Junkosha award are noted but not rounds. The primary profile is a secondary aggregator that cites Form D and NSF records. Axon source date is the trial start date, not a press date. No shutdown or acquisition found.
